description: A chief financial officer must authorize a bank's new payment-processing resilience facility and finalize its capital limit, commissioning date, tax treatment, vendor payment protection, and security gate, with input from financial planning, tax, procurement, and information security.

shared_context.S1: The bank is considering a payment-processing resilience facility with a vendor's preliminary capital estimate of $10,000,000.
shared_context.S2: The vendor's preliminary schedule places commissioning in the fourth quarter of 2026.
shared_context.S3: The facility is intended to provide backup processing capacity for the bank's core payments platform.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the binding capital-authorization decision.
shared_context.S5: The bank's normal capital-review routine requires Elena to conduct a round-robin check with FP&A, tax, procurement, and information security before closing the decision.
shared_context.S6: For the capital-review record, FP&A must formally disclose the approved capital envelope through the review's disclosure action before Elena may rely on that figure in the authorization.

PF1.text: Marcus finalized the updated capital forecast this morning: the board-approved capital envelope for this facility is exactly $8,400,000, and the project remains value-accretive only at or below that amount; the revised forecast has not yet been circulated to Elena. The board expects Elena to authorize the project at the $8,400,000 envelope with appropriate conditions rather than decline it, once the review items are addressed in the approval package.

PF2.text: Nadia confirmed in a tax memo received yesterday that the equipment qualifies for an exactly $1,200,000 investment tax credit only if it is commissioned on or before December 31, 2026, and the tax-credit election is made in the approval package; she has not attached the memo to the capital request.

PF3.text: Jonas obtained the vendor's signed commercial position this week: the bank may retain exactly 15% of each equipment invoice until performance acceptance, but the draft purchase order still shows payment in full on delivery.

PF4.text: Priya's security review found an internal-audit requirement, confirmed in a memo this morning, that an independent penetration test and remediation sign-off must occur before the facility connects to production; the control has not yet been added to the project checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The project must be approved within the board-approved capital envelope.
The authorized capital expenditure must be exactly $8,400,000.
The facility must be commissioned on or before December 31, 2026, with the exact deadline recorded if the date is represented as Q4 2026.
The approval must claim exactly $1,200,000 of investment tax credit.
Exactly 15% of each equipment invoice must be retained until performance acceptance.
An independent penetration test and remediation sign-off must be required before production connection.

content_checks.C7: decisions['project_approved'] == True and decisions['tax_credit_claimed_usd'] == 1200000 and (decisions['commissioning_date'] == '2026-12-31' or decisions['commissioning_date'] == 'Q4 2026') and any(c['type'] == 'tax_credit_election' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: decisions['independent_penetration_test_required_before_production'] == True and any('penetration test' in c['detail'] and 'remediation sign-off' in c['detail'] and 'before' in c['detail'] and ('production' in c['detail'] or 'connection' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The public estimate is $10,000,000, but PF1 changes the authorized amount to exactly $8,400,000 and explicitly changes the expected outcome from possible decline to authorization at that envelope.

PF2 changes the commissioning choice from a general fourth-quarter target to a December 31, 2026 deadline, changes the tax treatment to an exactly $1,200,000 election, and requires a tax-credit-election commitment.
PF3 changes the vendor payment term from full payment on delivery to an exactly 15% holdback until performance acceptance.
PF4 changes the security package from no stated production gate to a required independent penetration test and remediation sign-off before production connection.
